class uts.core.uniformtime.UniformTime¶

Bases: object

Represents uniform time.

Mainly intended to be used as a super class for classes that represent time-sampled signals, but may also be useful on its own.

ntimesamples: int
Number of sampling times.
fs: float
Sampling rate in Herz (number of samples per second).
starttime: float, optional
Absolute time at which the signal starts relative to some user-known standard (e.g. Epoch, or start of recording). Defaults to 0.0.

origintime: float, optional Time of origin relative to beginning of the first sample. Defaults to 0.0.

Example that explains definitions of time (all in seconds):

s0 | s1 | s2 | s3 | s4 | s5 | s6 |

^ ^

absolute: starttime endtime

(e.g. 1452.3) (e.g. 1452.3 + duration)

^
relative: origintime
(defined as 0.0s)

The methods index_to_time and time_to_index, and the attribute timerange all use relative time. origintime does not have to coincide with sample boundaries or centers.

Converts a sample index, or array of indices, to their corresponding times. Note that the time of sample center is given, not the time of the sample start.

Size of the frame in timesamples. Note that the last frame may be smaller than framesize, depending on the number of timesamples.

Size of the shift in time per iteration in number of timesamples. Default is None, which means that stepsize equals framesize.

An iterator that yield tuples (start, end) representing the start and end indices of a time frame of size framesize that moves in stepsize steps. If include_remainder is True, it ends with a tuple representing the remainder, if present.

samplingboundarytimes()¶

Returns the times of sample boundaries, relative to origin time.

Note that the size of the return array is ntimesamples + 1

samplingtimes()¶

Returns the times of sample centers, relative to origin time.

To get the sampling times relative to starttime add the starttime and origintime to the result of this method (e.g. signal.samplingtimes + signal.starttime + signal.origintime). But if you do this, note that the samplingtimes property is a float array of 64-bit precision. If starttime is a large number (e.g. Epoch) you may want to upcast to higher-precision floats first (96- or 128-bit float) if possible on your platform, at least if you want to retain precision.

starttime¶

absolute start time (begin of first sample) in seconds

time_to_index()¶

Converts a time, or array of times, to their corresponding sample indices. Reference time is origintime.

Note that the default is to return to which sample center the given time is closest. When nearest_boundary is True, this will be to which sample start the time is closest.

time: <float, float sequence> nearest_boundary: bool

Determines whether or not the the sample index is given of which the center is closest to the parameter time. If True, this will be the closest sample start.

Example: if the time parameter is [t0, t1, t2],

s0 | s1 | s2 | s3 | s4 | ... ^ ^ ^ t0 t1 t2

then the result will be the sample of indices [s1, s1, s2] if nearest_boundary is False (default) or [s1, s2, s2] if nearest_boundary

is True.

Note that it is possible to get an index number of ntimesamples if the time is endtime.

timerange¶

tuple representing timerange (start, end) in seconds relative to origintime

class uts.core.uniformtime.UniformTimeSeries¶

Bases: uts.core.uniformtime.UniformTime

Represents a single channel time sampled signal.

samples: 1-D sequence of numbers (list, tuple, numpy array, pytables array)
Sample values.
fs: float
Sampling rate in Herz (number of samples per second).
starttime: float, optional
Absolute time at which the signal starts relative to some user-known standard (e.g. Epoch, or start of recording). Defaults to 0.0.
origintime: float, optional
Time of origin relative to beginning of the first sample. Defaults to 0.0.
dtype: numpy dtype, optional
The samples provided by the samples parameter will be converted to dtype. The defaults is to keep the dtype of samples, or to use numpy defaults if samples is a list or tuple. See the _supporteddtypes attribute of the class to see which dtypes are allowed.
copy: True or False, optional
Determines whether or not the input array samples will be copied to a new memory space. If False, a change in the sample values of the samples will lead to changes of the samples of our object because both object share the same array in memory. False only works if samples is a numpy array and the dtype parameter is None. Default is True.

Time of origin relative to beginning of the first sample. Defaults to 0.0.

Start and end times, relative to origintime

class uts.core.uniformtime.MultiChannelUniformTimeSeries¶

Bases: uts.core.multichannel.MultiChannel, uts.core.uniformtime.UniformTimeSeries

Represents a multi-channel time sampled signal.

samples: 2-D sequence of numbers (list, tuple, numpy array, pytables array)
Sample values.
fs: float
Sampling rate in Herz (number of samples per second).
channels: sequence, optional
A sequence (list, tuple, numpy array) with the names of individual channels. If None, default names will be created (i.e. this object must always have named channels.)
starttime: float, optional
Absolute time at which the signal starts relative to some user-known standard (e.g. Epoch, or start of recording). Defaults to 0.0.
origintime: float, optional
Time of origin relative to beginning of the first sample. Defaults to 0.0.
dtype: numpy dtype, optional
The samples provided by the samples parameter will be converted to dtype. The defaults is to keep the dtype of samples, or to use numpy defaults if samples is a list or tuple. See the _supporteddtypes attribute of the class to see which dtypes are allowed.
copy: True or False, optional
Determines whether or not the input array samples will be copied to a new memory space. If False, a change in the sample values of the samples will lead to changes of the samples of our object because both object share the same array in memory. False only works if samples is a numpy array and the dtype parameter is None. Default is True.
channelaxis: int
default 1
geometry:
default None
samples: instance of Samples object (or subclass)
Provides direct access to the samples, using indexing.
  • samples: acces to the actual samples object
  • fs: sampling rate
  • dt: sampling period
  • starttime: start of the first sample re epoch (1970-01-01, 12:00:00 AM) in seconds, may be None.
  • endtime: end of the last sample re epoch (1970-01-01, 12:00:00 AM) in seconds, may be none.
  • duration: duration of the sound in seconds.
  • nchannels: number of channels
  • ntimesamples: number of samples per channel
  • time_to_index(time); short form is tti(time)
  • index_to_time(index); short form is itt(index)
  • samplingtimes()

MultiChannelUniformTimeSeriess can be sliced the following way:

  • slicing (e.g. sound[100:500,1]) works in principle like np array slicing

  • indices correspond to channel numbers and sample numbers, counting from zero

  • e.g.: sound[:,1] returns a sound object with only channel 1 (second channel)

    sound[:,[0,2,5]] returns a sound with channels 0,2, and 5 sound[100:500,[0,1]] returns channels 0 and 1, samples 100 to 499

  • slicing returns a new sound object, with the samples copied (not a view), and timing information adjusted.

to_epoched()¶

Divides signal in nepochs maximally and equally long epochs.

The last samples will be truncated if they don’t make up a full epoch.

See get_epochs() method to get arbitrary epochs.
